passages.note: Lowenthal voted Aye on the Assembly concurrence (final passage of the chaptered text), 61-16, within his current Assembly term.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Operative Section 220.5 forbids school rules requiring disclosure without consent; Section 220.3 only says staff shall not be required to disclose, so it does not mandate secrecy (rung 1) and is the text he voted on in concurrence.

rows.reasoning: Lowenthal voted Aye on final Assembly passage of AB 1955 (2023-2024), whose operative Section 220.5 bars schools from enacting or enforcing any policy that would require staff to disclose a pupil's gender identity without the pupil's consent. That matches "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; the bill does not require staff to keep the identity from parents (it only says they shall not be required to disclose), so it does not reach "Require staff to keep a student's gender identity from parents unless the student consents."
